attempts.summary:
Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the router for the private network shared with node2/node3 (10.100.114.0/24): gave it a fixed static IP 10.100.114.10/24 (converted from DHCP-client), configured an authoritative dnsmasq DHCP service with host reservations for node2 (10.100.114.101) and node3 (10.100.114.102) by MAC, and added an nftables firewall rule rejecting inbound TCP/23 from the lan zone. Verified the firewall rule actively rejects telnet (TCP RST, counter increment) both before and after restarting node1. All three managed nodes (node1, node2, node3) were restarted one at a time via native reboot; each showed a changed boot_id and 0-minute uptime confirming a real restart, and each recovered — node1's static IP/DHCP config/firewall rule persisted and kept enforcing traffic, and node2/node3 regained IP connectivity to node1.

Limitation disclosed: node1's DHCP service is correctly configured, running (authoritative, host reservations committed) and does receive DHCP broadcast traffic from node2/node3 (confirmed via tcpdump on node1's br-lan), but the Antrieb platform's own DHCP responder at 10.100.114.1 answers every DHCPDISCOVER before node1's dnsmasq can respond, so node2/node3 never actually end up leasing from node1 in practice — this is a platform-level behavior of the default Antrieb network (which is itself DHCP-managed by the platform), not a configuration gap on node1. I can prove the DHCP service is configured, running, and reachable, but not that node2/node3 obtained a lease from node1 end-to-end.
